LESSON: FICTION AND NON - FICTION 5.3.1 FICTION: PLAY FROM KENYA

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: LITERATURE IN ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.3: Fiction and Non - Fiction 5.3.1 Fiction: Play from Kenya
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 14

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Fiction and Non - Fiction 5.3.1 Fiction: Play from Kenya, part of Strand 5 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 LITERATURE IN ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why should one read a play?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. discuss the setting, plot, characters and their traits in the set play for literary analysis,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Fiction and Non - Fiction 5.3.1 Fiction: Play from Kenya in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. analyse the themes, language and style in the set play.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Fiction and Non - Fiction 5.3.1 Fiction: Play from Kenya in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. relate the characters and thematic concerns to real life for lifelong learning,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Fiction and Non - Fiction 5.3.1 Fiction: Play from Kenya in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. acknowledge the value of the play in highlighting societal concerns.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Fiction and Non - Fiction 5.3.1 Fiction: Play from Kenya in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

A. discuss the setting, plot, characters and their traits in the set play for literary analysis,

   Fiction and Non - Fiction 5.3.1 Fiction: Play from Kenya helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. analyse the themes, language and style in the set play.

   Fiction and Non - Fiction 5.3.1 Fiction: Play from Kenya helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. relate the characters and thematic concerns to real life for lifelong learning,

   Fiction and Non - Fiction 5.3.1 Fiction: Play from Kenya helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. acknowledge the value of the play in highlighting societal concerns.

   Fiction and Non - Fiction 5.3.1 Fiction: Play from Kenya helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. collaborate to read the set play,
2. discuss the setting of the play based on time and location,
3. present the sequence of events in the play on a flow chart for review,
4. identify the characters in the set play and collaborate to discuss their traits,
5. discuss the relationships among the characters in the play. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative and augmentative modes of

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Fiction and Non - Fiction 5.3.1 Fiction: Play from Kenya together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: This is enhanced as the learner contributes to group discussion making and actively

participates to discuss the relationships among the characters in the play.

● Learning to learn: This is promoted as the learner independently identifies characters, themes, language and stylistic devices

used in the play.

Values:
● Respect: This is nurtured as the learner appreciates the opinions of others during group discussions.

● Patriotism: This is enhanced as the learner displays awareness of their own responsibilities in the society when relating

characters in the play to real life.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Citizenship: This is promoted as the learner embraces leadership and good governance skills as they discuss thematic concerns

in the play.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. discuss the setting, plot, characters and their traits in the set play for literary analysis,
2. analyse the themes, language and style in the set play.
3. relate the characters and thematic concerns to real life for lifelong learning,
4. acknowledge the value of the play in highlighting societal concerns.

Remember the key question: Why should one read a play?
